title: Minimized Maximum of Products Distributed to Any Store
summary: Given an integer n indicating the number of specialty retail stores and an integer array quantities of length m representing the number of products of each of the m product types, distribute the products among the stores such that each store receives at most one product type.
statement: Given an integer n indicating the number of specialty retail stores and an integer array quantities of length m representing the number of products of each of the m product types, distribute the products among the stores such that each store receives at most one product type. The objective is to minimize the maximum number of products given to any single store. Return the smallest possible value of this maximum number of products.
constraints: There are at least as many stores as product types; quantities are positive.
Each store receives products of at most one type, while a type may be split among stores.
Minimize the greatest number assigned to any store.
reference_solution:
def minimized_store_maximum(n,quantities):
    low,high=1,max(quantities)
    while low<high:
        middle=(low+high)//2
        stores=sum((quantity+middle-1)//middle for quantity in quantities)
        if stores<=n:high=middle
        else:low=middle+1
    return low

hints: Feasibility is monotone in a proposed per-store maximum.
A type with q products needs ceil(q/limit) stores; binary-search the smallest limit whose total need is at most n.
If sum((q+m-1)//m)<=n move high=m, else low=m+1.
Any feasible larger limit remains feasible, and the ceiling count is both necessary and sufficient because types split independently.

tests.explanation: A maximum of three uses four stores for the first type and two for the second.
A per-store maximum of five distributes the types among seven stores.
